title: No outcome, no Brier: the totals market is left null by design
headline_insight: The MLB run-total market carries 2113 rescued in-game ticks but no resolved outcomes, so its Brier is reported null by design -- only the median model-vs-market divergence (0.116128) is disclosed, never a fabricated score.
what_it_means: Calibration only means something when predictions can be checked against what actually happened. Two market types carry settled outcomes and get scored (MLB moneyline: model 0.166759 vs market 0.151008; soccer match result: 0.332522 vs 0.195157). The totals quote-tracks were rescued from live data but never joined to a settlement, so scoring them would mean inventing labels -- instead only the disagreement is reported.
how_to_read: Each row is a market type; a real Brier appears only where has_outcome is true, otherwise the row shows n and a divergence stat with the reason it cannot be scored.
why_it_matters: It is a discipline demonstration -- the system refuses to manufacture a number it cannot back, which is the entire point of the calibration-first framing.
caveat: The divergence figure (median 0.116128 over 2113 ticks) measures how far the two forecasters sit apart, not accuracy -- with no outcomes it cannot say which side was right. The scored rows are revision 2, measured on the segment-clean corpus (27,351 MLB ticks, 4,265 soccer ticks).
